 Delaware Dems gain supermajority in House 
 Three seats flip on Election Day 
Rep. Alonna Berry is joined at the polls by Dionne Daisey-Williford, Attorney General Kathy Jennings and Evelyn Brady, Delaware Democratic Party state chair. BILL SHULL PHOTO 
 Nick Roth 
 November 3, 2026 
 Event Date: Tue, 11/03/2026 - 10:07 pm 
Rep. Alonna Berry is joined at the polls by Dionne Daisey-Williford, Attorney General Kathy Jennings and Evelyn Brady, Delaware Democratic Party state chair. BILL SHULL PHOTO 
 The Democratic Party will have a supermajority in both houses when the Delaware General Assembly reconvenes in January. 
 Entering the election, the Democrats held 27 of 41 seats, just one shy of the two-thirds needed for a supermajority. After the dust settled, they controlled 30 seats. 
 Republicans were unable to flip the two Cape Region seats, as Rep. Alonna Berry, D-Milton, defeated Republican challenger Gene Dvornick, and Rep. Claire Snyder-Hall, D-Rehoboth Beach, topped Republican candidate Mike Simpler. Neither race was particularly close. 
 "I am deeply grateful to the people of District 20 for trusting me to continue serving our community," said Berry. "This campaign has always been about neighbors helping neighbors. People opened their doors, shared their concerns, gave their time and showed up for one another."
 She thanked her volunteers, supporters and family for helping and sacrificing. 
 “Public service means showing up, listening and being accountable," Berry said. "The conversations we have had at kitchen tables, on doorsteps and in community spaces will continue to guide my work. I will keep turning those concerns into action for our families, our schools and our neighborhoods."
 In addition to her own victory, Snyder-Hall said she enjoyed the blue wave that took over the country in the national elections. 
 "I'm grateful voters in the 14th District put their trust in me for a second term," Snyder-Hall said. "There was a blue tsunami that sent a message to MAGA Republicans who attempted to meddle in the business of the states."
 Snyder-Hall said healthcare access and long-term care options will be priorities for her in the new legislative session. 
 The Democrats gained a seat in District 4, comprising the Long Neck and Millsboro area, as Gregg Lindner bested Republican Dan Zitofsky to replace Republican Jeff Hilovsky. Lindner, who unsuccessfully ran against Hilovsky in 2022, won 51.21% of the vote.
 " Thank you for placing your trust in me," Lindner told his constituents. "I’m deeply grateful to everyone who helped along the way, and I look forward to serving our District 4 community." 
 The Democrats also flipped the District 9 seat formerly held by  Kevin Hensley, as Ayanna Khan-Flowers easily defeated Republican Jamar Money, a nd  Annie Norman defeated Republican incumbent Lyndon D. Yearick in the Camden-Wyoming District 34. 
 Republicans retained four downstate seats with an incumbent and three newcomers. Rep. Bryan Shupe, R-Milford, defeated challenger Andy Gorlich in District 36, former Millsboro legislator John Atkins will return to the House to fill the District 41 seat of retiring Rich Collins with a six-point win over Ryan Stuckey, Carlie Carey will fill the Bethany Beach-area District 38 seat of retiring Ron Gray with a win over Maureen Madden, and Morgan Hudson, who won the primary by seven votes, will take Charlie Postles' District 33 seat in the Milford area with a convincing win over Joshua Pennington.  
 Change is coming to Sussex County Council, as Democrat Jill Hicks narrowly defeated Republican incumbent John Rieley in the District 5 race. Incumbent Doug Hudson staved off a challenge from Democrat Justine Cuccia in the District 4 race to ensure Republicans retain control of the five-member council. Hudson is the only incumbent to win in the last two election cycles, as three newcomers won seats in 2024.
 On the Senate side of things, the upper chamber will see a few new faces, but no change to the political ratio, as Democrats hold 15 of 21 seats. The only downstate newcomer is Republican Emily A. Thompson, who will take over the seat of retiring Republican Dave Lawson in the Marydel area. Senate Minority Leader Gerald Hocker, R-Ocean View, held onto his seat with a win over Harry S. Gold. Senate Minority Whip Brian Pettyjohn, R-Georgetown, ran unopposed. 
 There were no surprises in the statewide races, as the Democrats swept the board. Sen. Chris Coons won easily over Republican Michael Katz, and Congresswoman Sarah McBride won by a similar margin over Republican Joe Arminio. 
 Incumbents Kathleen Jennings and Lydia York will retain the attorney general and state auditor offices, respectively, while Ted Lauzen won by a comfortable margin to take over as treasurer. All statewide Democrats received more than 60% of the vote in their respective races. 
 The House Democratic Caucus met Nov. 4 to elect its leadership for the 154th General Assembly .   During the caucus reorganizational meeting, members selected Rep. Melissa Minor-Brown, D-New Castle, as speaker-elect; Rep. Kerri Evelyn Harris, D-Dover, as House majority leader; and Rep. Cyndie Romer, D-Newark, as House majority whip. The only change from the last session is Romer taking over as majority whip for Rep. Ed Osienski, D-Newark.  
 This year's election saw 384,862 people cast votes, or 47.49% of eligible voters. The 2024 election drew 65.74% of eligible voters to the polls. The last midterm election in 2022 saw 42.68% voter turnout.
 Nearly 130,000 people voted early, more than 20,000 voted absentee and more than 230,000 voted on Election Day.
